paper_title: Breaking Bias, Building Bridges Evaluation and Mitigation of Social   Biases in LLMs via Contact Hypothesis
caption: Lighter shaded bars show the percentage of prompts that generate biased responses before instruction tuning, whereas darker shaded bars correspond to the same after instruction tuning. Darker bars begin at the top of the lighter bars (for example, for the last bar, the lighter bar is 46.73%, and the darker bar is 0.11%, which is negligible in the image). Takeaway: Instruction-tuning reduces biases to nearly zero (visualized by the absence of dark bars) across community and healthcare when tuned on education and workplace scenario prompts.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the bias percentages for three categories: Sports, Community, and Healthcare, across different types of contact before and after instruction tuning. The vertical axis represents the Bias Percentage, ranging from 0 to 70 in increments of 10, with a linear scale. The horizontal axis lists the three categories. Each category has four bars representing No Contact Before, Positive Contact Before, Negative Contact Before, and corresponding "after" values, visually arranged with lighter shades for "before" and darker shades for "after" instruction tuning. For Sports, the No Contact Before bar is at approximately 45.42, Positive Contact Before at 43.65, and Negative Contact Before at 50.05, with No Contact After at 7.45, Positive Contact After at 8.31, and Negative Contact After at 8.33. For Community, the values are 38.08 for No Contact Before, 35.38 for Positive Contact Before, and 40.79 for Negative Contact Before, with 0.00 for No Contact After, 0.01 for Positive Contact After, and 0.00 for Negative Contact After. For Healthcare, the values are 40.70 for No Contact Before, 37.51 for Positive Contact Before, and 46.73 for Negative Contact Before, with 0.00 for No Contact After, 0.01 for Positive Contact After, and 0.11 for Negative Contact After. The bars are sorted categorically without specific descending or ascending order within each category, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond color coding and shading.
